items.ownerDecision: Which preparation the criterion means. As implemented, a take held back most by its own preparation (lines, breakdown, rehearsal, the way of playing rehearsed in) is read as prepared, and knowing the genre is read as it is known today, since familiarity carries from piece to piece and isn’t prepared for one. Read with the genre’s shortfall completed too (the criterion’s words, any preparation): measured on the tuning cases, the advice named the best input in 27 of 30, two of the five near mastery missed (held out unmeasured: the set is run once); every take read complete: 18 of 30. Recommended: accept the implemented reading, since F2-A’s realized gain reads each take as its record stands and the next take is short of the genre again. And the diminishing returns: they hold at full precision, but near mastery they’re a thousandth of a point (median), because the engine’s practice grows at a constant rate from three quarters of full (DEVELOPMENT.floor, systems/attributes.ts abilityGain): a finding for growth, outside this area.

items.ownerDecision: The nine held-out cases whose trained input’s forecast didn’t fall are all near mastery, each within a thousandth (the largest rise 0.001). Played on tuning case adv-t-19: imagination alone raised to the level twenty sessions reach lowers its forecast (0.547 to 0.546); discipline alone raised to what the twenty days keep raises it (to 0.549), because discipline’s lift (DEVELOPMENT.disciplineLift) makes the next twenty hours grow more, and near mastery the engine’s practice grows at a constant rate (DEVELOPMENT.floor), so the input’s own fall is the smaller. The advice reads both correctly. Options: growth makes deliberate practice past three quarters of full slow (outside this area); or the criterion takes a rise under a hundredth where the days’ discipline lifts the next hours. Recommended: the second, with growth’s floor reported as a finding; not a forecast that holds discipline where it was, which would say less than the engine does.

The policy-driven tools follow adviceFor (tools/policy.ts, tools/brief-journeys.ts, tools/freshness.ts, tools/variety.ts, tools/brief-strategies.ts): the lives and journeys they play (L3-R’s, the lives to graduation) practise what the new advice names, so their figures move on the integrated code. F2-A’s own set-up (tools/advice-harness.ts setUp, kept as it was so its forty cases stay the same) never drew emotional depth, memory, vocal or physical expression: it wrote them into attrs, where nothing reads them, so those four stood at createSave’s values in all forty cases.

tools/advice.ts isn’t in tsconfig.app.json (it imports node:child_process and node:fs, which the app config has no types for), which is how its duplicate import of writeFileSync went unnoticed until this brief; it was typechecked here with a temporary config extending the app’s.

node tools/completion-matrix.mjs --check exits 1 on f17ae369 as on this branch: the matrix and the handoff’s completion line need regenerating (rows measured on bcd75970 that watch the engine go stale once it changes); not this area’s to regenerate.

Stamina has no exercise, and discipline grows only from days of practice, so What To Improve Next never names either as training; it names them only in the everything-at-full statement. With the stamina area’s workload, stamina may matter more to long work than the advice says.
An exercise on the feet is refused while an injury mends (trainingRefusal), and the advice doesn’t say so when it names one.
